plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Southern Australia's bush and gardens glow with fluffy, honey-scented golden pom-poms. They cover the branches in such dense clusters that whole hillsides look as if they have been dusted with sunshine.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (peaking August to September)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, New South Wales, South Australia and the ACT
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. Wattle Day is celebrated on 1 September, right at the start of its peak flowering.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: Glossy, goblet-shaped golden flowers push straight out of dry, sun-baked ground, with no leaves yet. They look like crocuses in butter-yellow, and they brighten olive groves and rocky hillsides just as the first autumn rains return.
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe, Turkey and the Middle East through to Central Asia
plants.funFact: Despite its crocus-like look, it is a member of the amaryllis family. It is often called the 'harvester' because it blooms around grape-harvest time.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: Tall, arching plumes of tiny golden flowers rise above meadows and roadsides. They hum with bees, butterflies and beetles, and mark the turn from summer to autumn across the landscape.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, including old fields, prairies and roadsides
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often wrongly blamed for hay fever. Its pollen is heavy and sticky and is carried by insects, while the real culprit is ragweed, which blooms at the same time.
